title: OpenAIRE Graph — organization
cite_as: Manghi, P. et al. OpenAIRE Research Graph Dump (v3.0), Zenodo, 2021. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4707307
description: The **organization** slice of the 2021 OpenAIRE Graph: 277,330 research organisations as one range-queryable graph.
- One `oaire:Organization` per record, with legal name, short name, country code and website.

- Every organisation keeps its OpenAIRE id under `https://w3id.org/rete/openaire/20/…`. The converter would mint `https://ror.org/{id}` for a ROR id, but the 2021 dump identifies organisations by GRID, so this shard has none. That gap is left as it was published, so this file differs from the 2021 build only by the IRI repairs described below.

Source: the **OpenAIRE Research Graph Dump v3.0** (Zenodo [10.5281/zenodo.4707307](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4707307), published 2021-04-27, CC BY 4.0), converted to Parquet on 2026-07-15 with `scripts/openaire/tars_to_parquet.py` (19 source tars matched by name and size, zero bad lines), then to N-Triples by `scripts/openaire/parquet_to_nt.py --only organization`. Vocabulary `oaire:` = <https://w3id.org/rete/openaire#>.

Rebuilt with `rete build - --strict --memory-budget-mb 1500 --no-pyramid`. `--strict` refuses any IRI the N-Triples grammar or RFC 3987 rejects, so every IRI here loads into a strict triple store as-is. Website URLs (`websiteurl`) are percent-escaped where escaping keeps their meaning and repaired where the scheme is stated but mispunctuated (`http//www.uvs.edu`). They are **dropped and counted** when they carry no scheme (`www.sustech.edu.cn`) or when the repair still leaves an authority RFC 3987 rejects (`http//:hecon.uni-corvinus.hu`).
The converter prints its tally on every run. It never adds a scheme to a value that does not state one, and it never rewrites a host.
